descriptions.Monthly: Billing period: charged once a month. Not weekly.
descriptions.2,000 notes · 20 AI searches a day · 1 v: Free plan summary: three short items. Keep each ' · ' separator between them exactly as written.
descriptions.3,000 notes · 20 AI searches a day · 1 v: Free plan summary: three short items. Keep each ' · ' separator between them exactly as written.
descriptions.Read: Permission column header in a vault access table: the connection may read notes. A noun, not a verb.
descriptions.Write: Permission column header in a vault access table, next to the 'Read' column: the connection may change notes. Names the permission (a noun like 'write access'), never a command and never a Save button.
descriptions.the device on {os} that syncs your '{vau: Names an already-connected device (computer or phone) by the vault it syncs. A noun phrase, not a sentence.
Names an already-connected device (computer or phone) by the vault it syncs. A noun phrase, not a sentence.
descriptions.the device that syncs your '{vault}' vau: Names an already-connected device (computer or phone) by the vault it syncs. A noun phrase, not a sentence.
Names an already-connected device (computer or phone) by the vault it syncs. A noun phrase, not a sentence.
descriptions.monthly: Billing period, lower case: charged once a month. Not weekly.
descriptions.Edit access: Button that opens a dialog to change which vaults a connection can reach. An action (a verb phrase, like 'Change access'), not a noun.
descriptions.Edit access for {name}: Title of the dialog where the user changes which vaults the named connection can reach. An action (a verb phrase, like 'Change access for {name}'), not a noun.
descriptions.Revoke access: Destructive button that removes an app's access; must differ from Cancel, which sits next to it.
descriptions.Notes in {folder}: Heading over the notes inside a folder; {folder} is the folder's name.
descriptions.Reading view: Note view mode that shows the rendered note, read-only, as named in Obsidian.
descriptions.use {alias} or {key}: Help text under a note property: the user may type either name as the property key. {alias} and {key} are those names; keep both tokens.
descriptions.Reading: Note view mode that shows the rendered note, read-only, like Obsidian's Reading view.
